source_record.common_cost_and_alternative: Foregone output, scarce skill, reserve protection and shifted workload count. Stable low-variability service can use simple capacity and exception monitoring.
attempted_contrary_interfaces: First-tier diversity treated as independent lower-tier supply.
A complete document treated as operational capability.
A partial exposure or criterion input rejected for failing the whole receiver.
Capacity, stock or staff double-counted for routine and contingency use.
Buyer savings treated as joint fair gain.

positive_controls.argument: Queue age, arrival variability and actual throughput supply a loading condition for the timing/response contract and can expose a locally attractive but globally infeasible promise.
Actual bottleneck and queue behavior inform whether another increment increases active commitment or delays the next informative result, including the opportunity cost of keeping capacity idle.
Actual waiting, throughput and variability expose the error in treating local utilization or nominal labor hours alone as delivery capacity.
The end-to-end capacity picture identifies where supplier releases overload downstream work or where local output merely transfers a queue.
Observed workload and available response capacity provide a concrete premise for whether support can absorb startup variability and anomalies.
Protected capacity and queue behavior supply a resource/timing premise for recovery and expose whether urgent work will wait behind ordinary demand.
End-to-end waiting and capacity information expose whether maintenance/service obligations are being met or pushed into hidden backlog.
Queue and capacity evidence supplies the actual cost and response-opportunity side of a control package, including whether extra review delays urgent mitigation.
